7. Infrastructure:
a. The quality and capacities of existing infrastructure facilities have been found to be as follows: 
(1) Water supply is in adequate supply without danger of acquirer depletion.
(2) Sanitary sewage and solid waste collection is provided by the city. The facilities are adequate to handle the demand.
(3) Storm and sanitary sewers are combined. This is a city wide problem that is still under study. Within all redevelopment areas the storm and sanitary sewers will be separated. No flooding or drainage problems of any substance exist within the project area. The Randolph Plan has received the approval of the State Water Control Board. (See Appendix, Exhibit No. 4)
(4) Power can be supplied without problem.
(5) Local roads, and associated problem areas, have been discussed in detail. Most city streets within the conservation area are adequate.
b. Proposed Redevelopment Infrastructure and Their Impacts:
The infrastructure facilities will be redesigned and rebuilt within the redevelopment area. Separate sewer systems, underground power and telephone lines, and other of the items listed above will replace the inadequate facilities now existing.
Construction of the redevelopment area will be by sections. Sections will vary in size depending on relocation and available building area. No serious overload problems are expected. This expectation is primarily due to the fact that the population and density are expected to remain approximately the same after completion of the renewal activities as before them.
